 Karl-Anthony Towns accounted for 22 points (9-of-13 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 After struggling with early foul trouble in Tuesday’s loss to the 76ers, Towns did not commit a foul during the first quarter of Friday’s game. The bad news is that he made up for it by committing three fouls in the second quarter. Towns finished with a solid overall line, and avoiding early foul trouble let him log 37 minutes. He’ll look to build on Friday’s productive effort when the Knicks host the Magic on Sunday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Karl-Anthony Towns recorded a double-double on Tuesday with 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), 12 rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and three three-pointers against the 76ers. 
 KAT dealt with a ton of foul trouble early, which limited him to just six minutes in the first half. He played 18 minutes in the second half and was still able to turn in a strong stat line, though it was frustrating that he wasn’t available for most of the first half. That has been a bad habit of KAT’s at times throughout his career, but it isn’t something that should happen every game. He’ll look to fix that against the Celtics on Friday. 
 Karl-Anthony Towns 
 NYK 
 Center-Forward 
 #32 
 Karl-Anthony Towns finished Monday’s exhibition against the 76ers with five points (2-of-4 FGs), five rebounds and two assists. 
 Towns recently expressed displeasure with how his contract negotiations with the Knicks have gone, but he also vowed professionalism won’t be an issue. The 7-footer has a player option worth $61 million for the 2027-28 campaign, but closing a deal before the season starts would likely save the Knicks money. With Josh Hart and Miles McBride also hoping to get deals done, the Knicks have some financial things to address as they look to repeat as champions. 
 Karl-Anthony Towns 
 NYK 
 Center-Forward 
 #32 
 Karl-Anthony Towns’ contract negotiations with the Knicks have stagnated and a deal before training camp is unlikely, reports ESPN’s Shams Charania. 
 Charania’s report aired on ESPN Wednesday afternoon. Towns is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million max extension. According to a report from Stefan Bondy of the New York Post, the Knicks are asking Towns to take less than the max, which explains how the negotiations have seemingly fallen apart. Towns’ stock will likely never be higher coming off a championship run where he was arguably the second-best player on the team. He’s coming off the board in the early part of the second-round of fantasy drafts. 
 Karl-Anthony Towns 
 NYK 
 Center-Forward 
 #32 
 Karl-Anthony Towns recorded two points (1-of-7 FGs), 10 rebounds, one assist, three steals and one block in Saturday’s Game 5 win over the Spurs. 
 For the second consecutive game, Towns struggled with foul trouble on Saturday. While he was productive as a rebounder and defender in his 23 minutes, extended bench time robbed KAT of his offensive rhythm. However, this did not keep the Knicks from winning their first NBA title since 1973. And even with the poor individual finish, Towns’ play throughout New York’s title run may boost his value in fantasy drafts. The Knicks were most lethal when more of the offense ran through KAT, which may be an approach head coach Mike Brown takes in 2026-27. Using a late-first round pick on Towns in standard league drafts would not be a reach.

 Karl-Anthony Towns added 13 points (4-of-5 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 10 rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Spurs. 
 Towns battled early foul trouble in Game 4 but showed up for his team when it mattered most. He logged just 18 minutes but scored a couple of big baskets in the fourth quarter as the Knicks mounted their comeback, and finished the period as a team-best plus-21. The veteran center earned his third double-double of the series despite the low minutes total on Wednesday. He’ll have an opportunity to tally a fourth when the Knicks attempt to close out the Spurs on Saturday.

 Karl-Anthony Towns had 21 points (8-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 13 rebounds, four assists, one block, one steal and three three-pointers in the Knicks’ 105-104 victory over the Spurs in Game 2 on Friday. 
 As the teams left the floor for halftime at the end of the first half, cameras caught Towns letting everyone know that Victor Wembanyama can’t mess with him. He continued to back up that talk in the second half with his second double-double of the series. Towns isn’t close to being dominated by Wembanyama the way the Thunder’s Chet Holmgren was in the Western Conference finals. The way he’s playing right now, he’s closer to having a legitimate chance of winning Finals MVP.

 Karl-Anthony Towns generated 18 points (7-of-15 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Spurs. 
 Towns’ biggest moments of Wednesday’s contest came in the third quarter, scoring 10 points in the frame while helping overcome a 14-point deficit to tie the game at 76 at the period’s end. He didn’t score in the final frame, but still concluded the game with solid numbers. The veteran center had several nice drives and finishes at the basket while being defended in isolation by Victor Wembanyama. If he can continue to hold his own in that matchup, the Knicks could find themselves in favorable positions.

 Mitchell Robinson (finger) is questionable to play against the Spurs in Game 1 of the NBA Finals on Wednesday. 
 Previous reports indicated that Robinson should be available, and he was able to do some individual work on Sunday. However, his official designation for the first game of the Finals is questionable. Don’t expect Mike Brown to dip deep down the depth chart for center minutes if Robinson is out. Karl-Anthony Towns will likely play a massive workload, with Ariel Hukporti giving him a few minutes to breathe when Victor Wembanyama isn’t on the floor.

 Karl-Anthony Towns had 19 points (8-of-11 FGs), 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals, two blocks and three three-pointers in the Knicks’ 130-93 victory over the Cavaliers in Game 4 on Monday. 
 Towns was efficient with 19 points on 11 attempts in Game 4 as the Knicks completed a sweep of the Cavaliers and advanced to the NBA Finals for the first time in 27 years. Towns was +25 in 26 minutes as New York dominated from the start of the game, leading by 19 points at halftime. The Knicks will have eight full days off before the NBA Finals, where they’ll face the winner of the Western Conference finals. 
 Karl-Anthony Towns 
 NYK 
 Center-Forward 
 #32 
 Karl-Anthony Towns amassed 13 points (4-of-9 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, seven assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s Game 3 win over the Cavaliers. 
 Towns came out hot in Game 3, scoring 11 of the Knicks’ 37 first-quarter points. He would only score three more points the rest of the way, but the ability to facilitate for others was once again on display. Towns recorded a team-high seven assists in Game 3, and he was also responsible for eight rebounds and three steals. While Cleveland’s Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen have put up decent numbers, Towns has been the best post player in the Eastern Conference Finals. The Knicks will look to complete the sweep with a win in Game 4 on Monday.

 Naz Reid had 17 points (7-of-16 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Reid had seven turnovers despite only playing 24 minutes and that’s a crusher in nine-category leagues. Otherwise, he’s scored 37 points on 15-of-34 attempts with seven three-pointers in his first two games with the Hornets. That’ll play. If Reid can keep the turnovers under control, he’s well on his way to paying off his mid-round draft price.

 McBride rebounded nicely from his poor showing in Tuesday’s loss to the 76ers, a game in which he scored three points on 1-of-5 shooting.  Jalen Brunson accumulated 19 points (7-of-17 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Brunson’s gotten off to a slow start by his standards, shooting 13-of-32 from the field in New York’s first two games. The Knicks star also didn’t shoot well from the foul line, missing three of his six attempts in Boston. Those rostering Brunson don’t have much to worry about, as the season is only two games old. However, they would certainly like to see him clean up his shooting in Sunday’s game against the Magic.

 Jalen Johnson had 19 points (9-of-16 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, eight assists, three steals and one block in Friday’s game against the Hornets. 
 With less than two minutes left in the first half, Dyson Daniel hit the floor for one of his seven steals, leading to a Jalen Johnson alley-oop dunk on the other end. That pretty much encapsulates how the night went for the Hawks as Johnson led the team in scoring with 19 in the 128-81 blowout win. Johnson showed he was able to move past the extracurriculars with the Magic on Wednesday with his usual excellent performance against the Hornets.

 After scoring 10 points on 3-of-12 shooting in Tuesday’s loss to the 76ers, Anunoby was much better offensively on Friday. An 8-of-10 night at the foul line boosted his point total, and the Knicks forward shot just under 50 percent from the field. Add in the rebounds and assists, and this was a solid night for those rostering Anunoby.
